title: Backend mid scenario idempotent payment retry
topic: Backend mid scenario idempotent payment retry
question: A client calls POST /charge to charge a customer's card, the request times out on the client side, and the client automatically retries. How do you make sure the customer isn't charged twice?
idealAnswer:
Recognizes that a client-side timeout doesn't tell you whether the server-side operation actually completed, so simply 'not getting a response' can't be trusted to mean 'nothing happened'

Proposes an idempotency key: the client generates a unique key per logical charge attempt (not per HTTP request) and sends it with every retry, the server stores which keys it has already processed and returns the original result instead of charging again

Explains the storage needs to be checked and written atomically (e.g. a unique constraint on the idempotency key in the database) so two near-simultaneous retries can't both slip through the check

Considers what to return while the original request is still in flight (not yet finished) when a retry with the same key arrives, so the retry doesn't race ahead of the original

Mentions that many payment processors support idempotency keys natively, and a strong answer would pass the same key through to the processor as well, not just dedupe at the API layer
